description.value: A retrospective study investigated the natural history and symptom progression of temporal variant frontotemporal dementia in patients with left versus right temporal lobe atrophy, using structural MRI regional volume measurements and clinical records.

spans.text: In this study, we examined clinical records to estimate first symptoms and the timing of subsequent symptoms in quantitatively defined patients with left- and right-sided tvFTD.

description.value: Retrospective observational study of patients with temporal variant frontotemporal dementia, with left and right temporal lobe variants compared using structural MRI and clinical records.

name.value: ipsilateral versus contralateral regional brain volumes

definition.value: ROIs were designated as ipsilateral or contralateral, using the side of worst temporal atrophy as the point of reference, and Z scores were subjected to paired-sample t tests.

value: In both groups, the ipsilateral temporal lobe was the most atrophied region, significantly more so than the contralateral temporal lobe and ipsilateral amygdala. The contralateral temporal lobe was more atrophied than the ipsilateral and contralateral ventromedial frontal cortices and contralateral total frontal cortex.

definition.value: Between-group differences in ipsilateral and contralateral ROI Z scores were assessed using independent-sample t tests.

spans.text: Thus, between-group differences in ipsilateral and contralateral ROI Z scores were assessed using independent-sample t tests.

value: The groups were well matched for ipsilateral and contralateral temporal atrophy. The only region that differed between groups was the ipsilateral amygdala, which showed more atrophy in RTLV than in LTLV.

name.value: regional brain volumes correlated with disease duration

definition.value: Disease duration was tested for a negative correlation with volumes in individual ROIs.

value: Anterior temporal volumes strongly and inversely correlated with disease duration. Ipsilateral ventromedial frontal volume showed a trend in the same direction, whereas no other ROI was significantly related to disease duration.
